title: Recover from cwd-scoped zero by widening

request.question: In flow-conformance evaluation, what does an UNKNOWN deterministic row mean, and how does it affect score denominators?

ground_truth.initial_scope_proof: A raw search constrained to git:github.com/AI-Substrate/flowspace3 and crates/** at min-score 0.60 returned ok=true, count=0, and next_action explicitly said to widen.
ground_truth.global_answer_address: el:git:github.com/AI-Substrate/harness-engineering/docs/how/flow-conformance-eval.md::Flow-conformance evaluation::Reading the numbers — the statistics behind a report::Three-valued rows and where `unknown` goes
ground_truth.global_resolution: The global address returned ok=true via flowspace3 get at span [287,298].
source_facts: UNKNOWN means the evidence channel was unavailable, not that the subject failed.
UNKNOWN rows are excluded from every score denominator.

stability.reason: The answer is durably owned by another repository, but the initial scoped zero can rot if flowspace3 later documents the same evaluation rule.
stability.refresh_trigger: Re-prove both the scoped zero and the global address before each committed baseline refresh.
